title: Rim Light
description: Rim lighting is a narrow edge of light, usually from a flagged backlight, that separates a subject from the background without opening the face. The highlight sits on brim, hair, and coat; flesh stays mostly dark.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: The shot becomes a graphic: a profile or three-quarter figure drawn with a thread of exposure. You keep just enough flesh to know it is a person, not a paper doll.
Crime, spy, and night-city work use it so a body reads against wet asphalt or a black wall. It is the wrong tool for a dialogue close-up that needs both eyes.
If the rim fattens into a cheek slash, you have a kicker. If the whole figure goes empty and the sky is the subject, you have a silhouette.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Use a small hard source behind the subject, slightly off to one side, with flags or a snoot so the beam only kisses the outline. Keep it out of the lens unless you want veil.
Color is often white or slightly cool against a warmer dim key, or warm against night blue. Do not wrap to the front plane of the face.
Prompt: Photographic backlight on [Subject] from behind, a thin natural highlight on hat brim, hair, and coat edge, faces staying dark. Not a neon outline.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it for a graphic night figure, a spy on a roof, a coat against a black street. Do not use it when the audience must read a mouth for a line.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Backlight is the broader rear direction; rim is the thin result. Kicker hits cheek, jaw, or shoulder as a hard side-back accent with more flesh.
Hair light lights only the hair from above-behind. Silhouette removes the edge highlight and exposes for the ground instead.

sections.title: In film

blocks.text: Blade Runner rims figures in smoky interiors so coats and hair hold against black. Skyfall uses thin natural rims on night exteriors, faces kept dark, outlines readable.
Those are edges from sources, not stickers.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a neon outline or a full silhouette. The tell is a glowing closed stroke around the body, or no highlight at all.
Fix it by attaching a thin highlight to hair and cloth only, from a real rear source.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is rim light in film?
A narrow edge of light that separates the subject from the background. The face stays dark; brim, hair, and cloth catch the highlight.
Rim light vs kicker
A rim traces the outline. A kicker is a harder side-back slash on jaw, cheek, or shoulder, with more flesh in the accent.
When should I use rim light?
Use it when shape matters more than expression, and a dark figure must still unstick from a dark ground.
How do I prompt rim light for AI image or video?
Specify a thin natural highlight on hair and coat from behind, face remaining dark, no neon outline. Name the rear source.
